title: NEBIUS_API_KEY still reaches every CLI child through the shared spawn door
body:
## Summary
Every claude and codex child the daemon spawns still inherits NEBIUS_API_KEY, a key no CLI owns, because the Proving Ground spawns its own Python child through the same child_env door and that child needs the key.

## Description
subscription-auth-selection: a secret a child legitimately needs is passed by name to that child only, and a child that reads untrusted content gets no secret it does not own. child_env (src/athena/harness/transports.py:96) now strips every CLI engine's billing key (5ff9504) but names none for nebius (src/athena/harness/transports.py:88). Stripping NEBIUS_API_KEY there turned tests/proving/test_server.py::test_no_secret_in_any_response red: src/athena/proving/server/runner.py:539 builds the run child's env with proving.roles.claude_env (src/athena/proving/roles.py:229), i.e. the CLI door, and that child calls Nemotron. Fixed looks like: the runner builds its child's env itself (allow-list or child_env plus NEBIUS_API_KEY by name), then ENGINE_KEYS['nebius'] names the key and every CLI child loses it.

## Flow
- daemon env carries NEBIUS_API_KEY (the nebius engine, ADR 0031)
- SubprocessTransport.run -> child_env(os.environ, ...) -> claude/codex child sees NEBIUS_API_KEY
- the child reads fenced page text; an indirect instruction that gets it to print its environment has one more secret to print
- fix in build order: runner.py passes the key by name to its own child; ENGINE_KEYS['nebius'] = ('NEBIUS_API_KEY',); add it to the test's ENGINE_KEYS

## Expected impact
Nobody sees a difference in a working run; the exfiltration surface of every CLI child shrinks by the one key the build pays per token for. Could break: a proving run that loses the key, which the proving server test catches.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - no CLI child sees a key it does not own
Before: probe: a real child spawned through SubprocessTransport sees NEBIUS_API_KEY (the first red run of the 5ff9504 test listed it among 6 visible keys)
After: predicted 0 keys visible, with tests/proving/test_server.py green
Method: simulation - the After needs a change in src/athena/proving/server/runner.py, another context's file
Result: better
Gate: policy-tighten
evidence: src/athena/harness/transports.py:88 `"nebius": (),` ; src/athena/proving/server/runner.py:539 `env = {k: v for k, v in claude_env(self.environ).items() if k != TOKEN_ENV}` ; tests/proving/test_server.py:546 `assert "generating: the key is [redacted]" in joined` went red when child_env stripped NEBIUS_API_KEY (this round, before 5ff9504 was narrowed)
instrument: tests/harness/test_subprocess_exit.py with NEBIUS_API_KEY added to its ENGINE_KEYS (red today) plus tests/proving/test_server.py green, after runner.py builds its child's env with the key by name

title: A parent Claude Code session's markers reach the claude CLI the daemon spawns
body:
## Summary
When the daemon runs inside a Claude Code session (a developer or an agent running athena serve), the parent's session markers, a messaging token among them, ride into every claude child the daemon spawns.

## Description
subscription-auth-selection, 'Session nesting is part of auth hygiene': the door strips the vendor's session markers alongside the billing keys, so the child starts as a fresh top-level session; agent-runtime-assembly/nested-run-is-not-its-parent: a child must not inherit the parent's session identifiers through the environment. child_env (src/athena/harness/transports.py:96) strips only billing keys. This round's own shell carried CLAUDECODE, CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID, CLAUDE_CODE_CHILD_SESSION, CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT, CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ATTENDED, CLAUDE_CODE_MESSAGING_SOCKET, CLAUDE_CODE_MESSAGING_TOKEN, CLAUDE_CODE_EXECPATH, CLAUDE_PID and CLAUDE_EFFORT. Fixed looks like: a dated, named marker list beside ENGINE_KEYS, stripped by child_env; never a CLAUDE_CODE_* prefix, which would also strip real configuration (CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN, CLAUDE_CODE_GIT_BASH_PATH).

## Flow
- an agent runs athena serve from inside Claude Code
- a turn -> SubprocessTransport -> claude -p with the parent's CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID and CLAUDE_CODE_MESSAGING_TOKEN
- the child may treat itself as nested, or attach to the parent's messaging socket; the parent's token is in a process that reads untrusted pages
- fix: verify the marker list against claude 2.1.x, strip it at the door, pin it with the real-child env test

## Expected impact
Developers and UAT agents who run the daemon from Claude Code get a child that starts clean; end users running the desktop app see no change. Could break: a marker the child needs, which is why the list must be verified and named.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - a spawned claude never inherits its parent session's identity
Before: 10 CLAUDE_* session variables present in this round's shell; child_env passes all 10 (only billing keys are stripped)
After: predicted 0 session markers in the child, with claude -p still starting
Method: simulation - which markers change claude's behaviour is not documented here, and the live comparison spends tokens
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: policy-tighten
evidence: `env | grep ^CLAUDE` in this round's shell: CLAUDE_CODE_CHILD_SESSION, CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID, CLAUDE_PID, CLAUDE_EFFORT, CLAUDE_CODE_MESSAGING_SOCKET, CLAUDECODE, CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ATTENDED, CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT, CLAUDE_CODE_EXECPATH, CLAUDE_CODE_MESSAGING_TOKEN ; src/athena/harness/transports.py:93 STRIPPED holds only the six billing variables
instrument: a named marker list verified against claude 2.1.x docs, pinned by a real-child env test in tests/harness/test_subprocess_exit.py; plus a live claude -p init record compared with and without the markers (operator, spends a turn)

title: Every codex turn persists its whole prompt, page text included, on disk
body:
## Summary
codex exec saves a session file for every Athena turn, holding the constitution, the host state, recalled memory and fenced page text, although Athena never resumes a codex thread.

## Description
Data retention: a store of more than the product needs. CodexDialect.argv (src/athena/harness/cli_harness.py:261) passes exec --json --skip-git-repo-check -s read-only and no --ephemeral; the dialect is resumes=False (src/athena/harness/cli_harness.py:295), so the saved thread is never read by Athena. codex-cli 0.160.0 documents `--ephemeral  Run without persisting session files to disk` (codex exec --help, 2026-10-16). Athena's turns also fill the person's own `codex resume` picker. Fixed looks like: --ephemeral in the codex argv at or above the codex version it was verified on, which needs the probe's version to reach the dialect (dated-capability-matrix); an older codex that does not know the flag would fail every turn.

## Flow
- a codex turn: codex exec --json ... - with the frame on stdin
- codex writes the rollout under ~/.codex/sessions/<date>/
- nothing in Athena reads it; it stays on disk with page content in it
- fix: a version-gated --ephemeral from the dated capability table

## Expected impact
The person's disk stops accumulating copies of every page Athena read through codex, and their codex history stops filling with Athena turns. Could break: every codex turn, on a codex older than the flag, if the gate is wrong.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - an engine that is never resumed keeps no transcript on disk
Before: 1 session file per codex turn (codex default; ~/.codex/sessions exists on this machine)
After: predicted 0 per turn at or above the verified version
Method: simulation - counting files needs a live codex turn (spends the person's plan)
Result: better
Gate: policy-tighten
evidence: src/athena/harness/cli_harness.py:261 `argv = ["exec", "--json", "--skip-git-repo-check", "-s", "read-only"]` ; cli_harness.py:295 `resumes=False` ; `codex exec --help` (codex-cli 0.160.0): `--ephemeral  Run without persisting session files to disk` ; `ls ~/.codex/sessions` -> 2026/
instrument: a dialect test that argv carries --ephemeral only at/above the verified codex version (the probe's version threaded to the dialect), plus a count of ~/.codex/sessions files across one live codex turn with and without it (operator)

title: A codex error record mid-stream fails the turn even if the turn then completes
body:
## Summary
CodexDialect.decode reads every `error` record as a failed result, and the harness keeps the first failed record as the outcome, so a codex run that reports a transient error, retries and finishes would still end the turn as an error.

## Description
output-normalization: classify the run's outcome, not its first complaint. src/athena/harness/cli_harness.py:283-286 maps `turn.failed` and `error` alike to Decoded('result', is_error=True); src/athena/harness/cli_harness.py:387-390 keeps a failed record as the outcome 'even if a later one says otherwise'. If codex exec --json emits `error` for a stream retry (a reconnect notice) and then `turn.completed`, the answer is thrown away and the person sees an engine_error. Fixed looks like: only `turn.failed` (and an `error` with no later `turn.completed`) is terminal. Whether codex 0.160 emits `error` for retries is the open premise.

## Flow
- codex exec --json: thread.started, error {message: reconnecting...}, item.completed agent_message, turn.completed
- decode -> result(is_error) then result(ok)
- _invoke keeps the failed one -> classify -> engine_error; the reply is dropped

## Expected impact
Codex users stop losing answers to a transient hiccup the CLI itself recovered from. Could break: a genuinely failed run that also printed turn.completed.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - a run the CLI recovered is not reported as failed
Before: unknown - no recorded codex transcript with a retry exists in tests/fixtures
After: predicted: the recovered run streams its answer
Method: simulation - the premise needs a real capture, and a live run spends the plan
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: none
evidence: src/athena/harness/cli_harness.py:283 `if kind in ("turn.failed", "error"):` ; :286 `return Decoded("result", is_error=True, said=_text(message))` ; :387-390 `A failed record stays the outcome even if a later one says otherwise.`
instrument: a captured `codex exec --json` transcript of a run that reconnected mid-stream, replayed through ScriptedTransport into CliHarness (operator capture)

title: A name or tool parameter written beside an explicit action is dropped silently
body:
## Summary
When a model writes its parameters at the top level of an op that names its action, a parameter called `name` or `tool` is discarded, so the call reaches the gate without it.

## Description
op_grammar treats name and tool as envelope keys always (src/athena/harness/op_grammar.py:85), but they carry envelope meaning only when there is no action (the name_field_names_tool repair). params_at_top (src/athena/harness/op_grammar.py:214-217) therefore drops them: parse_op('{"op":"propose_action","action":"host.crm.add_contact","name":"Bob","email":"b@x.io"}').params == {'email': 'b@x.io'}, and with `name` alone params is {} and no repair is recorded. ADR 0050 lists name and tool among the envelope keys, so the fix amends it. Fixed looks like: with an explicit action and no params, a name or tool whose value is not tool-shaped is a parameter.

## Flow
- model writes OP: {"op":"propose_action","action":"host.crm.add_contact","name":"Bob","email":"b@x.io"}
- parse_op -> params {'email': 'b@x.io'}, repairs (params_at_top,)
- the catalog validates a call without its name: refused 'missing name', or run without it when name is optional

## Expected impact
A contact, file or record created through a page tool keeps the name the model gave it. Could break: an op that repeats a non-tool-shaped name beside its action, which would now carry an extra parameter a strict validator refuses.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - every parameter the model wrote reaches the gate
Before: probe: 1 of 2 parameters kept in the example above; 0 of 1 with name alone
After: predicted 2 of 2 and 1 of 1; the cost is unknown without the bench's op lines
Method: probe - the parser figure is measured; whether the change helps or hurts real runs needs the recorded bench transcripts
Result: better
Gate: contract
evidence: src/athena/harness/op_grammar.py:85 `_ENVELOPE_KEYS = frozenset({"op", "action", "params", "rationale", "name", "tool"})` ; :214 `stray = {k: v for k, v in data.items() if k not in _ENVELOPE_KEYS}` ; probe this round: params {'email': 'b@x.io'} and {} ; docs/adr/0050-name-field-and-top-level-params.md Decision lists name and tool as envelope keys
instrument: count, over the recorded bench and proving transcripts, OP envelopes carrying name/tool beside an action (tool-shaped or not), then a grammar test both ways and an ADR 0050 amendment

title: Unknown sign-in reads as found, and doctor calls signed-out 'no credential'
body:
## Summary
After ADR 0118 the probe's logged_in is the CLI's own verdict or None for unknown, but GET /engines renders None as `found`, and athena doctor still explains False as 'no credential was found'.

## Description
availability-probe: unknown renders as unknown, never as either neighbour. src/athena/daemon/routes.py:1178 maps only logged_in False to not_logged_in, so None (a check that could not be read) is `found`. src/athena/cli.py:175-176 says '<engine> <version>, but no credential was found' for False, which for a verified CLI now means its own check said signed out, credential file or not. The desktop's EngineState already has `unknown` (apps/desktop/src/lib/engines.ts:25), but there it means 'the probe has not answered yet' (engines.ts:15), so reusing it would merge two facts; the wire needs a decision. Fixed looks like: a wire state (or detail) for 'installed, sign-in unknown', mirrored in api.ts, and the doctor's sentence saying 'signed out'.

## Flow
- a verified claude whose auth status cannot be parsed -> logged_in None
- engine_row -> state found -> setup says ready
- athena doctor on a signed-out CLI with its file present -> 'no credential was found' while the file is there

## Expected impact
Setup stops calling an unverified sign-in ready, and the doctor's line names the cause the probe found. Could break: the desktop's readiness rules if a new state is added without its mirror.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - the wire and the doctor say what the probe knows
Before: 2 consumers of logged_in (routes.engine_row, cli._engine_stage) collapse None into found/ok; 1 sentence names a cause the probe no longer checks
After: predicted 0 of each
Method: simulation - both sites are in other contexts (daemon, cli, desktop)
Result: better
Gate: contract
evidence: src/athena/daemon/routes.py:1178 `if status.logged_in is False:` ; src/athena/cli.py:176 `f"{engine} {status.version}, but no credential was found"` ; apps/desktop/src/lib/engines.ts:15 '`unknown` is the probe not having answered *yet*'
instrument: a routes.engine_row test for logged_in None with the chosen wire state, its api.ts/engines.test.ts mirror, and a doctor stage test for the signed-out sentence
